final_candidates.decision_summary: Catalytic PLP-anchoring lysine; highest phenotype LOF score (0.987) with low evolutionary tolerance and low plausibility, all consistent with abolished activity. Best-supported candidate for loss-of-function.
Active-site cysteine with high phenotype score (0.926); serine substitution removes the catalytic thiol. Strong, concordant multi-tool evidence for LOF.
Catalytic histidine with strong phenotype score (0.845); alanine substitution removes general acid/base functionality. Retained over T191M (0.716) based on stronger LOF evidence.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool has converged: the top three candidates show consistent, high LOF evidence across phenotype, plausibility, and conservation tools, and further evidence gathering would not change the final ranking.

history.rationale: Lys119 forms the internal aldimine (Schiff base) with the pyridoxal phosphate cofactor; replacing it with alanine abolishes PLP anchoring and catalysis. Central, highly conserved residue, so loss is near-certain while the protein can still fold.
K119 is the conserved PLP Schiff-base lysine; alanine substitution should abolish PLP anchoring and thus catalytic activity.

Alphamissense LOF proxy 0.987 (pathogenic) for the PLP-binding catalytic lysine; low PLM plausibility and low evolutionary tolerance are consistent with severe functional disruption rather than mere instability.
Catalytic PLP-anchoring lysine; highest phenotype score (0.987) with low MSA tolerance and low plausibility, all consistent with LOF.

Cys52 is the heme axial ligand in the N-terminal heme-binding domain; substitution is a classic route to destabilize the PLP-dependent catalytic machinery. Serine preserves size/polarity, limiting gross misfolding while disabling heme coordination.
Cys52 is part of the heme-binding cysteine pair; mutation disrupts heme binding, strongly impairing but possibly not fully abolishing activity.
Pathogenic 0.926 at the catalytic cysteine–polysulfide/PLP-site residue; Cys-to-Ser removes catalytic chemistry while preserving fold, fitting the LOF objective.
Conserved active-site cysteine with high phenotype score (0.926); serine substitution abolishes the catalytic thiol.

His65 coordinates the heme iron; alanine removal disrupts heme binding, which allosterically impairs CBS activity. Removing a histidine ligand is a well-tolerated structural change but a strong functional hit.
His65 coordinates the heme iron; removing it destabilizes heme-dependent catalytic machinery, though residual PLP-dependent activity may persist.
Promoted to rank 3: alphamissense 0.845 (pathogenic) at an active-site histidine, whereas C272S was predicted benign (0.317) and is demoted.
Catalytic histidine with strong phenotype score (0.845); alanine substitution removes the general acid/base functionality.

T191 is a well-established recurrent pathogenic missense variant in homocystinuria causing loss of CBS function. The conservative T->M change preserves viability while impairing the active-site environment.
T191M is a documented pathogenic homocystinuria mutation with strong LOF association, but structural/active-site mutations (K119, C52) are more direct.
Pathogenic 0.716 near the catalytic pocket, kept as backup but below H65A.
Moderate phenotype score (0.716); viable backup but inferior to top three.

R125 lies adjacent to the catalytic core and is a reported pathogenic CBS variant (pyridoxine-responsive LOF). Glutamine partially preserves charge distribution, keeping the enzyme stable but functionally compromised.
Active-site pocket residue; R125Q is a known homocystinuria-associated missense change likely reducing activity, but partial activity retention is plausible, so downranked.
Benign phenotype score (0.153) and poor mechanistic rationale; rejected.

rejection.reason: Benign phenotype score (0.153) and poor mechanistic rationale; rejected.

history.rationale: R266K is one of the most frequently observed pathogenic CBS mutations (common in European homocystinuria patients). The conservative substitution retains folding viability while sharply reducing activity.
Conservative lysine substitution near the catalytic site likely preserves substantial activity; poor choice for full LOF.

rejection.reason: Conservative lysine substitution near the catalytic site likely preserves substantial activity; poor choice for full LOF.

history.rationale: Alternative disruption of the PLP Schiff-base lysine: arginine retains positive charge and size but cannot form the internal aldimine, ablating catalysis. Slight risk of residual non-covalent PLP binding reduces confidence versus K119A.
Conservative substitution that may partially retain PLP interaction; inferior to K119A for abolishing activity.

rejection.reason: Conservative substitution that may partially retain PLP interaction; inferior to K119A for abolishing activity.

history.rationale: C272 lies adjacent to the PLP-binding lysine in the active-site loop; serine substitution is expected to severely disrupt catalysis — pending verification with tools.
Alphamissense classifies C272S as benign (0.317), contradicting the hypothesis that this adjacent-loop substitution abolishes activity; demoted below H65A and T191M.
Hypothesis of active-site disruption failed: phenotype score is only 0.317, indicating the substitution is not strongly damaging; drop from final pool.

rejection.reason: Hypothesis of active-site disruption failed: phenotype score is only 0.317, indicating the substitution is not strongly damaging; drop from final pool.
